title: A 3D-Printed GHz Microwave-Resonator Paul Trap for Electron Confinement and Millisecond Spin-Qubit Coherence
authors: Niklas V. Lausti, Vineet Kumar, Ivan Hudák, Jiří Hajnyš, Peter Kúš, Radek Plašil, Michal Hejduk
abstract: We report a 3D-printed microwave-resonator Paul trap that operates at the GHz frequencies required for electron confinement while preserving an open geometry suitable for laser access and imaging ion Coulomb crystals. The resonator exhibits moderate quality factors of approximately 1000, enabling large confining electric-field amplitudes at low input power, and is in good agreement with finite-element-method (FEM) predictions despite manufacturing imperfections, which we experimentally characterize. The validated FEM model is then used to calculate the electromagnetic fields in the trapping region. These field distributions, together with surface-roughness measurements, are incorporated into a model of electron spin-qubit decoherence to estimate the coherence time. Our analysis predicts that electron spin-qubit coherence times on the order of 10 ms should be achievable under the assumption that motional heating is dominated by Johnson noise, making such systems relevant for quantum information processing. The method of obtaining the coherence time is applicable to any electron Paul trap.
summary: The paper presents a novel, 3D-printed microwave-resonator Paul trap designed for confining electrons at GHz frequencies while preserving optical access. By characterizing the trap's electromagnetic fields and modeling decoherence, the authors predict that the device can achieve electron spin-qubit coherence times of about 10 ms, advancing the feasibility of quantum information processing using trapped electrons.
main_problem: The authors address the challenge of creating a trapping platform that can simultaneously confine electrons using high-frequency microwaves while maintaining an open geometry necessary for optical access and imaging.
main_result: They report a 3D-printed microwave-resonator Paul trap capable of operating at GHz frequencies, predicting electron spin-qubit coherence times on the order of 10 ms.
method: The study combines experimental characterization of the trap's electromagnetic properties (using resonance measurements) with theoretical modeling (FEM and decoherence analysis) to predict qubit performance.
model_or_system: The system is a 3D-printed microwave-resonator Paul trap, which functions as a dual-frequency trap for confining both electrons and ions. The dynamics are modeled using the electron spin Hamiltonian coupled to the motional degrees of freedom, and decoherence is analyzed using master equations.
key_observables: Resonance frequency (2.3 GHz), Quality Factor ($Q \approx 10^3$ measured), Electron Spin-Qubit Coherence Time ($\sim 10 	ext{ ms}$), Trapping Frequencies ($\omega_x, \omega_y, \omega_z$).
important_parameters: GHz operating frequencies, moderate $Q$ factor, surface roughness ($	ext{R}_{qp} \approx 2.5 \mu	ext{m}$), and the assumption that motional heating is dominated by Johnson noise.
main_assumptions: The coherence time prediction assumes motional heating is dominated by Johnson noise, and the analysis relies on the accuracy of the 3D-printed structure's electromagnetic response.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the trap design (outer cavity body and central resonator rod) and show surface profilometry/SEM images comparing polished vs. unpolished samples, confirming surface quality.
paper_structure: The paper details the design and fabrication of the 3D-printed trap, characterizes its electromagnetic response via resonance measurements, models the trapping potential and nonlinear dynamics (Kerr parameter), and finally uses these results to estimate the electron spin-qubit coherence time.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the engineering challenge of integrating high-performance microwave confinement with optical access, a critical bottleneck for scaling up quantum memories based on trapped particles.
